Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

lifr (development version)

Second round of daktools ports

Six more defects carried over from the daktools October/November 2026 fixes (daktools issues #791, #792, #801, #795, #661, #647). Two changed what a figure claimed about the data:

  • lif_overview() and qc_compare() gain ymin, and say what falls below the value-axis floor (daktools #661). coord_flip(ylim = ) zooms rather than drops, so every row stayed in the layer data, ggplot emitted no “Removed n rows” warning, and a reading below the floor was drawn on the panel edge, reading as zero. That mattered most for hp: with the default water_table = 0, hp_correction() subtracts the full hydrostatic column from the ground surface, which the function itself warns over-corrects the unsaturated zone – on the bundled demo site that puts 101 of LIF-06’s 150 readings as low as -2.64 psi, and the 0 floor turned them into a flat trace against the axis that reads as “very permeable” rather than “correction artifact”. ymin defaults to 0, so no existing figure changes shape; what is new under the defaults is the disclosure, a message of class "lifr_below_floor" and a one-line panel caption (“101 readings below 0”). ymin = NULL floors at min(0, 1.05 * min(value)) and marks 0 with a thin line. The LIF panels keep their 0 floor: negative %RE is not a quantity. qc_compare() discloses on every channel, signal included – it is a QC view of what an edit changed, not a log display.
  • boring_map(fill_floor =) greys a detect below the screening floor, and process_site() passes the report’s floor (daktools #801). The response map gave a boring at 0.3 %RE a full-strength emission colour while chart_max_response(), a page away in the same report, greyed that same boring’s bar – so two figures in one deliverable disagreed about whether a boring carried a product signature. A grey marker keeps its size and its detect status: the reading is real, it just carries no colour claim. Default NULL is the old look.
  • lif_zero_below_threshold(borings =) records which borings it edited (daktools #791). Scoped to a subset, it wrote a single audit row with boring = NA, which the report reads as “every boring at the site” – putting the whole-log caption under logs the edit never touched. It now writes one row per named boring, each with its own n_rows_changed, as lif_zero_shallow() already did. Called without borings it still writes the one boring = NA row, because there that is true. A name repeated in borings is one target, not two.
  • qc_compare() marks a reading it can no longer plot, and no longer drops a one-sided depth (daktools #795). A depth whose value is NA in edited – what lif_editor(value = NA) writes – was detected as a change, but geom_point() had no y to draw and silently dropped the mark, so the panel pair looked identical. Those depths now get a red cross just above the panel floor and a subtitle saying so. The depth match is also an outer join now: a depth present in only one frame, which is what lif_downsample() leaves behind, was excluded from the comparison entirely and could report a changed boring as unchanged.
  • process_site()’s step log formats each correction argument on its own (daktools #792). The detail string was built with paste(names(p), unlist(p), sep = "="), which recycled the argument names over the flattened values, so any argument longer than one value shifted every later one: hp = list(water_table = c("LIF-01" = 12, "LIF-02" = 14.5), gradient = 0.433) was logged as water_table=12; gradient=14.5; water_table=0.433, putting a 14.5 ft/ft gradient on the record and contradicting the edit history in the same report. Vectors now render as c(LIF-01=12|LIF-02=14.5) and lists as list(a=1|b=c(2|3)). Scalar-only details are unchanged.
  • ?new_edited_data now states the real edit-history survival rules (daktools #647). Three places claimed rbind() concatenates histories unconditionally. It does so only when its first argument carries a lifr class: rbind()’s dispatch takes the first argument whose class has a method and data.frame has one, so rbind(plain_df, edited) falls to rbind.data.frame and returns an unclassed frame with no history at all – not even the edited argument’s – and nothing warns. Also newly stated: dplyr::bind_rows() keeps at most the first argument’s history and never merges two, and as_tibble()/as.data.frame() drop the class rather than the attribute, so the banner stops printing while edit_history() still reads it. Verified by execution and pinned by test, so an upstream change reads as “re-verify the docs” rather than as a lifr regression. No behaviour changes.

First round of daktools ports

Defects ported from the daktools October/November 2026 fixes (daktools issues #662, #666, #667, #649, #789, #796). Three of them changed what a figure claimed about the data, so figures regenerate:

  • boring_map(): marker area is now proportional to peak signal, and the map carries a size key (daktools #662). The old law kept a 40 % diameter floor, which drew a boring at 1 % of the site peak at 7.8 % of the peak’s area (10 % at 20 %, 25 % at 36 %), with no key to read sizes against – a ring of weak detects around a hot spot read as a broad moderate plume. The maximum-signal marker keeps the diameter it had (2 * point_size); every other marker shrinks to its honest area. The hollow non-detect ring is off the size scale and is never larger than the smallest detect. nd_threshold must be >= 0 when size_by_signal = TRUE; size_by_signal = FALSE is unchanged. Suppress the key with ggplot2::guides(size = "none").
  • chart_max_response(): the caption now names only the encodings the bars carry (daktools #667). It used to claim “bar colour = emission colour at peak-signal depth” over every chart and fill the colour-less bars a muted olive – a plausible fluorescence hue – so a delivery with no colour channel shipped a false caption over bars that read as real signatures. A bar above the screening floor with no usable colour is now hollow.
  • Area fills break at NA instead of running straight across the gap (daktools #796). Since ggplot2 3.4 geom_area() defaults to stat_align, which drops NA rows and interpolates, so an interval deleted with value = NA was painted as signal while the line over it broke correctly. Affects lif_plot(), lif_plot_all(), qc_compare() and the report’s channel panels.
  • lif_plot_all(layout = "facet") draws the per-reading emission colour and the colour strip, as layout = "list" already did (daktools #666). The sheet ignored color entirely, so the comparison a small-multiples sheet exists for – which borings share a fluorescence signature – was the one thing it could not show. Colour is decided per boring; a frame with no colour renders exactly as before.
  • lif_keep() now errors when the keep window contains none of the boring’s readings (daktools #789), instead of silently zeroing the whole boring – the feet/metres and decimal-slip guard. lif_apply_edits() checks every keep row before applying any of them. A delete window that changes 0 readings raises a classed warning ("lifr_edit_noop") naming the boring, the window and the boring’s depth range; lif_zero_shallow() muffles it, since a boring with nothing left to zero is expected there.
  • export_site_charts() reports a chart it could not build or save instead of skipping it like an absent channel (daktools #649). Both used to return NULL, so the report embedded the previous run’s PNG and process_site() logged the survivors as the complete set. Each failure now warns, lands in the returned value’s "failed" attribute and gets its own process_site() log row, the other charts still render, and a stale PNG at a failed chart’s path is deleted. A builder returning NULL because the site has no data for that chart is still a silent skip.

lifr 0.1.1

Fixes from the September 2026 code review (issues #1-#20). Behaviour changes worth knowing:

  • lif_read() / lif_import(): trailing delimiters on data lines no longer shift every column (#1); digits-only colour codes keep their leading zeros (#2); a header-only log is omitted with a warning instead of aborting the import (#3); read_locations() aliases (x, y, id, …) never overwrite a canonical column (#4).
  • hp_correction() indexes a per-boring water_table by name even when boring is a factor (#5); new_lif_data() converts factor borings to character.
  • The edit history now survives [, rbind() (histories concatenate), and the dplyr verbs (#6). merge() and as_tibble() still drop it.
  • n_rows_changed counts readings whose value changed, not readings inside the window, so re-applying an edit records 0 (#7). The editors’ default bottom is now Inf rather than 1000.
  • process_site(corrections = list(hp = FALSE)) skips the correction (#8). A failing summary, chart, or report step raises a warning and is logged as failed even with quiet = TRUE (#11).
  • NA-depth readings are left alone by every editor; lif_zero_shallow() also masks readings above ground surface; a keep plan row needs at least one bound (#9).
  • The Markdown report escapes paths and names, so Windows paths no longer break the PDF (#10). The logs PDF is written before the Markdown that links to it and is removed if it fails; unrenderable figures leave a visible placeholder (#18). TinyTeX installs off PATH are detected.
  • compat_rename_legacy() warns on every collision, not once per session (#12). lif_simulate() restores the caller’s RNG state (#13).
  • qc_compare() pairs repeated depths correctly; re_feet() averages repeated depths; lif_downsample() keeps NA-depth rows; summarize_lif() handles a 0-row frame and reports unbinned readings (#14).
  • The report’s change detection matches readings on depth (#15). boring_map() gains min_extent so one boring or a collinear transect keeps a sensible window, and labels are formatted per element (#16). chart_ec_histogram() leaves outliers out of the histogram and states them in the caption (#17). The HTML report has proper tab and header roles, keyboard-sortable tables, and a hash handler that cannot throw (#19). theme_lifr() honours base_size; depth_slice_map(agg_fn=) receives a plain vector; the basemap featureless check ignores the alpha plane (#20).

lifr 0.1.0

Initial public release.

  • lif_read() / lif_import() read .lif.dat.txt / .csv logs (modern header layout and headerless legacy 11- and 16-column layouts), keep every source column, and join a locations table via read_locations().
  • Editors with an audit trail: lif_editor(), lif_editor_bulk(), lif_keep(), lif_zero_shallow(), lif_zero_below_threshold(), lif_apply_edits(), and the edit_history() accessors.
  • Processing: hp_correction(), re_feet(), lif_downsample().
  • summarize_lif() QA statistics.
  • Plots: lif_plot(), lif_plot_all(), lif_overview(), qc_compare(), boring_map() (with fetch_basemap() imagery), depth_slice_map(), and the chart_*() site charts with export_site_charts().
  • process_site() pipeline and site_report() renderer: self-contained HTML, Markdown, PDF, and a per-boring logs PDF.
  • lif_simulate() synthetic site generator; the bundled demo dataset is built with it.
  • Documentation: a getting-started guide plus articles on the raw file format, editing with an audit trail, a plot gallery, and the site report; README with rendered example figures.
